title: Starc's 10-Wicket Demolition Ends Mackay Test in Two Days as Australia Level Series
excerpt: Mitchell Starc took 10-51 as Bangladesh were bowled out for 64 and 95 at the Great Barrier Reef Arena, tying the historic series 1-1.
body:
• Mitchell Starc took match figures of 10-51, including 6-12 in the first innings, as Australia demolished Bangladesh by an innings and 51 runs inside two days at Mackay.
  • Bangladesh were bowled out for 64 and 95 after their historic nine-wicket victory in the first Test at Darwin, leaving the series tied 1-1.
  • The match was the first Test ever played at the Great Barrier Reef Arena, and the third Australian Test in the past seven to finish within two days.
  • Bangladesh's Shoriful Islam produced a career-best 7-48 but could not prevent the collapse as Australia's pace attack proved devastating on a bouncy wicket.

Starc Strikes From Ball One

Mitchell Starc produced one of the most devastating spells of his career as Australia crushed Bangladesh by an innings and 51 runs inside two days at the Great Barrier Reef Arena in Mackay on Sunday, tying their two-match series 1-1.

The left-arm paceman struck with the first ball of the match to remove opener Shadman Islam and went on to take five wickets in just 22 deliveries — the sixth-fastest five-wicket haul in Test history. He already holds the record for the fastest, having taken five in 15 balls against the West Indies in Kingston last year.

Starc finished the first innings with figures of 6-12 as Bangladesh were skittled for 64. By the end of the match, he had 10-51, sweeping both the Player of the Match and Player of the Series awards with 12 wickets at an average of 12.08 across the two Tests.

"What we expect of ourselves this week is what we got, particularly with the ball and the wicket that aided us with the ball."

— Mitchell Starc, Player of the Match

A Devastating Collapse

Bangladesh's first innings lasted barely a session. Starc removed openers Shadman Islam and Tanzid Hasan alongside captain Najmul Hossain Shanto and wicketkeeper Litton Das — all for ducks. Captain Pat Cummins added 3-25, bowling Mushfiqur Rahim for five and having Mehidy Hasan Miraz caught in the slips.

Australia's reply of 210 was modest but more than enough. Cameron Green, whose place in the side had been questioned during the Ashes, top-scored with a composed 67 before being trapped lbw by an in-swinging yorker from Shoriful Islam. Tailender Nathan Lyon frustrated Bangladesh with an unbeaten 32.

Shoriful Islam was the standout for Bangladesh, finishing with 7-48 — the best innings haul by a Bangladesh bowler in an away Test. But his effort was overshadowed by his team's batting failures.

Second Innings No Better

Trailing by 146 runs, Bangladesh's second innings followed the same pattern. Starc took two wickets in successive balls early on, removing Shadman Islam for one and bowling Mominul Haque for a duck. Shanto offered brief resistance with 31 before miscuing a lofted drive off Nathan Lyon to hand Starc an easy catch at long-off.

Bangladesh were dismissed for 95 in 38.3 overs, bringing the match to a close before tea on day two. Lyon took three wickets in the match while Cummins added two more in the second innings.

A Series of Contrasts

The Mackay result stood in stark contrast to Darwin, where Bangladesh produced one of Test cricket's greatest upsets. They piled on 426 runs in their first innings on a flat wicket before bowling Australia out to win by nine wickets — their first Test series in Australia in 23 years yielding a result nobody predicted.

"We showed our character and our discipline in that first test and we need to be consistent," Shanto said after the Mackay defeat, calling for more regular tours to Australia. "Not long, long time — like 23 years. And then play two test matches. It's not easy."

Cummins acknowledged the turnaround. "We needed to bounce back and it was a great couple of days from the lads," he said. "If we get a really good first hour or two, we can set up the rest of the match."

Pitch Concerns and What's Next

The Mackay Test was the venue's debut as a Test ground, but its Gabba-style pitch drew scrutiny. Three of Australia's last seven home Tests have finished within two days — a pattern that has cost Cricket Australia millions in forgone gate revenue.

Australia now face reigning World Test Championship holders South Africa in a three-Test tour in October, where their batting frailties — only Green passed 50 in Mackay — will face a far sterner examination.
nri_angle: The Mackay Test adds to a growing pattern of ultra-short Test matches in Australia, raising questions about pitch preparation that resonate with cricket fans across the Indian diaspora ahead of Australia's tour to India in early 2027.
